chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:

A man mortgages barren land (which bears no fruit); he cultivates it and spends from his own wealth on it. Indeed, his expenses and his labor are considered purely his own. Then he looks at the share of the land and accounts for it from the wealth with which he mortgaged the land, until he has fully recovered his capital from his wealth. When he has recovered his capital, he should return the land to its owner.

key_terms.اَلْبُور: Barren land that bears no fruit

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on mortgaging barren land and how are cultivation costs handled?
ai.summary: Reported by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) from Imam Ali (AS), this hadith clarifies the fiqh of rahn (mortgage) regarding barren land, distinguishing between the recovery of the principal debt value and the retention of cultivation profits by the mortgagee. It establishes a fair economic principle where the mortgagee bears the risk and reward of labor, ensuring the debtor is not penalized for the creditor's productive efforts, a ruling foundational to Shia commercial jurisprudence.
